lines: Eve CEO Jay Madheswaran argues AI's real impact on plaintiff law is revenue expansion, not cost-cutting: firms are limited by legal labor rather than client demand, and the show says they turn away up to 96% of potential cases.
He says AI agents that run the full case lifecycle, from intake to settlement and often 10,000+ individual actions, can let firms handle up to five times more cases without proportional hiring.
In his view, legal software is really a 'shadow labor market', making its addressable market far larger than traditional software metrics suggest.

He argues insurers' centralized, automated claim-denial systems create a data asymmetry that AI-equipped plaintiff firms can now counter, with attorneys becoming data-scientist-like designers of agent workflows.
Madheswaran expects contingency law's outcome-based model to spread to other legal areas, and future firms to scale by hyper-specializing in specific fact patterns backed by proprietary data.
title: Why AI Could Turn Small Law Firms Into Billion-Dollar Businesses
